text:
Camille: Heads up — acme-corp reported a hard failure on our /v1/generate path this morning. They started getting 400/500s after we rotated their customer CMK yesterday. API error bubbled up as: "InvalidCiphertextException: EncryptionContextMismatch". Also they saw a billing spike from retries. Posting minimal repro + logs we have.

Nora: Which deployment is this on (hosted/dedicated/private)? any key ARN?

Camille: Dedicated (private VPC) — key ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/0a1b2c3d-EXAMPLE. Service role is redwood-dedicated-encryptor@acct. Rotation happened ~2026-11-02 03:15 UTC.

Samir: Can you paste the KMS decrypt log / CLI output? EncryptionContextMismatch usually means the Encrypt call used a different context (or none) than the Decrypt.

Camille: Here is the decrypted error we get from the runtime when handling the request (redacted):

```
2026-11-03T10:22:14Z ERROR runtime.kms decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertextException: The ciphertext refers to a different encryption context.
	at runtime.kms.Decrypt(…)
	request_id=cli_0a3f…
```

And the raw CLI repro against their blob (we ran this in a debug container):

```bash
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cipher.blob --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/0a1b2c3d-EXAMPLE \
  --encryption-context ClientId=acme-corp,Env=prod
# -> InvalidCiphertextException: EncryptionContextMismatch
```

Nora: Did the Encrypt calls include an encryption-context? CloudTrail will show Encrypt/Decrypt events — check the requestParameters.encryptionContext on the encrypt event. If encrypt had no context but decrypt expects one (or vice versa) you get this.

Samir: I looked at CloudTrail for that key: the Encrypt events from before rotation show requestParameters.encryptionContext = null for many objects; after rotation our service started sending ClientId=acme-corp. So some objects were encrypted without a context (legacy objects) and others with context. Decrypt fails when the provided context doesn't match what was used to encrypt.

Ryan: Two failure modes here: (1) key rotation replaced the underlying key material (ok) but our code assumed every blob has the same encryption context and now some older blobs don't — so Decrypt with context fails; (2) the key policy/grants may not include the new key material/service principal. We need to check both.

Samir: Quick checks to run (put in repro checklist):
- aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-arn>  # ensure redwood role has a GRANT with Decrypt allowed
- aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key-arn>
- CloudTrail: lookup Encrypt events for acme-corp object prefix and inspect requestParameters.encryptionContext
- run aws kms decrypt against a failing blob with and without the --encryption-context to confirm mismatch

Camille: list-grants output: no grant for redwood-dedicated-encryptor — only the root account and an older service principal. So the new key material doesn't have a grant for our service role. I think our rotation process created a new CMK alias pointing to new key version and forgot to re-grant the role.

Nora: That would explain the Decrypt failing even when context matches for newly encrypted blobs — but the EncryptionContextMismatch points to context mismatch for older blobs specifically. So both issues present.

Samir: Immediate mitigation options:
- Option A (fast): create a new grant for redwood-dedicated-encryptor on the current CMK so Decrypt calls by our service succeed for blobs encrypted with that key material. Command: 

```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-arn> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-dedicated-encryptor \
  --operations Decrypt --name redwood-dedicated-grant
```

- Option B (longer): for blobs encrypted without any context, perform a backfill re-encrypt pipeline: Decrypt (no context) -> Re-encrypt with standard encryptionContext map (ClientId,Env,Version). That requires access/permission to decrypt those legacy blobs (we can do this with a maintenance job).

Ryan: Also update key policy to automatically allow the service role on future rekey/rotation events, or bake grant creation into rotation workflow. Right now rotation step missed creating the grant.

Camille: Support note — customer also reported a billing spike because their client retried 5x on our 5xxs. We should include an apology and note on ETA to fix.

ops-bot: [incident-tracker] linked incident INC-2026-1123 created by Camille. Priority P2.

Samir: Proposed concrete plan:
1) eng-infra: run create-grant for redwood-dedicated-encryptor on the active CMK (owner: @Samir) — immediate (ETA 30m).
2) eng-ml/infra: run CloudTrail scan job to enumerate legacy objects encrypted without context and produce a list (owner: @Nora) — ETA 2 hours.
3) infra: schedule a re-encrypt job for legacy objects with careful throttling and monitoring (owner: @Ryan) — ETA next-day.
4) devex: update rotation playbook to include grant recreation and add a rollback checklist (owner: @Camille) — ETA 3 days.
5) support: message customer with root cause and mitigation plan + credit for retries (owner: @support-bot) — immediate.

Nora: Small note — we must be careful with re-encrypt: if the legacy blobs truly have no context we must pass none to decrypt. If we attempt decrypt with a context we will fail. The re-encrypt job should attempt decrypt first without context, then if that fails try with the expected context set (ClientId=acme-corp,Env=prod,Version=1), log results and escalate mismatches.

Camille: OK I'm going to create the grant now and open a support message. Will post results here. :thumbsup:

Samir: If grant creation doesn't immediately fix all errors, post a failing request_id and I'll run a live repro in the staging VPC with the customer's blob.

support-bot: Drafted message to customer: "We identified a key rotation grant misconfiguration and inconsistent encryption context usage across stored objects. We're creating a grant for our service and running a re-encryption job for older objects. We'll follow up with ETA and a credit for retry costs."

Camille: grant created -> create-grant returned GrantId: a1b2c3d4. Observing fewer errors in logs already, but one problematic object still failing (request_id=cli_0a3f-legacy). Attaching blob id to the incident.

Ryan: Good. Next: Nora to run CloudTrail scan and produce object list, Samir to prep re-encrypt job. Support to send customer update. I'll add the rotation-playbook task to backlog. :eyes:

Nora: Scan in progress — found ~1.2k objects encrypted pre-context. Starting safe re-encrypt run in staging now.

Camille: Thanks team. Keeping INC-2026-1123 open until re-encrypt completes and customer confirms no more retries.

Samir: Postmortem notes to include: rotation automation must recreate grants; enforce a schema for encryptionContext (required keys + casing rules); add CI test that simulates rotation and validates service principal grants.

Camille: Agreed. Closing loop after re-encrypt.
